settings.name: Cinnamomum cassia (bark) Extract
settings.role: The primary active. Supports healthy blood sugar levels and insulin sensitivity, which helps reduce post-meal glucose spikes: the spikes that drive fat storage signaling and cravings.

settings.name: Japanese Knotweed Extract
settings.role: A natural source of trans-resveratrol. The Japanese heritage ingredient and metabolic driver of the formula. Supports metabolic health, antioxidant activity, and healthy inflammatory response.

settings.name: Bitter Melon Extract
settings.role: Traditionally used across Asia for metabolic support. Supports healthy blood sugar metabolism and glucose utilization.

settings.name: Extract of Turmeric Root
settings.role: Antioxidant support and healthy inflammatory response, which plays a role in overall metabolic function.

settings.name: Extract of Licorice Root
settings.role: Traditionally used to support digestive health and adrenal function; may support healthy cortisol levels and metabolic balance.

settings.name: Matcha
settings.role: Natural antioxidants (EGCG catechins) that support gentle thermogenesis and a metabolic boost without stimulant jitters.

settings.name: Glycerin
settings.role: Natural carrier for botanical extracts, adds slight sweetness

settings.title: Cinnamomum cassia: blood sugar and insulin sensitivity
settings.citations:
Wickenberg J, et al. "Cassia cinnamon does not change the insulin sensitivity or the liver enzymes in subjects with impaired glucose tolerance." Nutrition Journal, 2014.
Anderson RA, et al. "Cassia Cinnamon Supplementation Reduces Peak Blood Glucose Responses." Journal of the American College of Nutrition, 2015. Found reduced peak post-meal glucose response.
"Mechanistic and clinical insights into the antidiabetic potential of Cinnamomum cassia." ScienceDirect review, 2025. Mechanism review on insulin secretion and sensitivity via cinnamaldehyde.

settings.title: Japanese Knotweed (Polygonum cuspidatum): resveratrol and metabolic health
settings.citations:
"Resveratrol and cardiovascular health." ScienceDirect, 2014. Trans-resveratrol sourced from P. cuspidatum; cardiovascular and metabolic risk reduction.
"A Comparative Evaluation of the Antioxidant Ability of Polygonum cuspidatum Extracts with That of Resveratrol Itself." MDPI, 2024. Antioxidant activity confirmation.

settings.title: Bitter Melon (Momordica charantia): glucose metabolism
settings.citations:
Kosin University (Korea): 12-week randomized controlled trial on prediabetic participants. Bitter melon extract reduced post-OGTT blood glucose via suppressed glucagon response. NCBI/PMC, 2023.
Note: a 2024 Frontiers in Nutrition systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 pooled RCTs found mixed, non-significant results; the literature is genuinely contradictory, so on-page claims stay measured.

settings.title: Turmeric (Curcuma longa): inflammation and metabolic support
settings.citations:
"Effects of dietary polyphenol curcumin supplementation on metabolic, inflammatory, and oxidative stress indices." Frontiers in Endocrinology, systematic review and meta-analysis, 2023.
"Targeting Inflammation-Induced Obesity and Metabolic Diseases by Curcumin and Other Nutraceuticals." PMC. Mechanism review on adipocyte and pancreatic interaction.

settings.title: Licorice Root: cortisol and adrenal support
settings.citations: Restorative Medicine Journal: review on Glycyrrhiza's inhibition of 11-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase, the enzyme that breaks down active cortisol. Mechanism for supporting cortisol availability.

settings.title: Matcha (EGCG): thermogenesis
settings.citations:
Hursel R, et al. "The effects of catechin rich teas and caffeine on energy expenditure and fat oxidation: a meta-analysis." Obesity Reviews, 2011.
"Effect of Acute and Chronic Dietary Supplementation with Green Tea Catechins on Resting Metabolic Rate, Energy Expenditure and Respiratory Quotient." PMC systematic review, 2021. 15 studies, 499 participants.
